messages:
mara: FYI I pushed a lightweight dashboard prototype showing prompt-cache warmup SLO sampling by model + customer. Wanted early feedback before I add slices for routes and token-saved.

mara: The goal is to answer: are we getting expected warmup hit-rate within the first N requests (per route/model/customer)? and what amount of tokens saved accrues during warmup.

dennis: Nice. Can you share what the sampling window is and how you compute "warmup" vs steady-state?

mara: Current heuristic: first 30 requests per (model, route, customer) are considered warmup. We use reservoir sampling to keep a representative prefix sample and compute cumulative hit-rate over that window.

olivia: 30 seems fine as a starting point. For small customers that may not have 30 reqs/day though. Do you bucket by time too?

mara: Yep — two dims: (1) N-requests warmup window and (2) time window fallback (30m since first seen). We mark warmup done when either condition satisfied. The dashboard exposes both metrics so you can toggle.

sre_jen: How are you quantifying token-saved? Is it per-token or approximate? Need to be careful for reporting and SLOs.

mara: Token-saved = sum_over_requests(prefix_len * hit_flag) where hit_flag=1 if prefix matched and we reused KV cache. We also show effective token-saved normalized by total tokens to avoid skew from high-throughput customers.

data_khan: Quick question — are you slicing by kernel-selection variant? Sometimes we route to an int8-quant variant for cost and that has different latency/hit dynamics.

mara: Good call. I included a dropdown for model_variant (fp16 / int8 / int4) — the cache keying should be identical across variants for the same model id, but kernel runtime differences show up in the latency pane.

dennis: Can you paste the PromQL/SQL used to compute the warmup hit-rate? Want to review before it goes into grafana.

mara: Sure, here's the core query skeleton (Prometheus-ish):
```
# fraction of warmup requests that hit cache per (model, route, customer)
sum by (model, route, customer) (increase(prefix_cache_hits{env="prod"}[30m]) and on(model,route,customer) increase(request_count{env="prod"}[30m])) \/ 
sum by (model, route, customer) (increase(request_count{env="prod"}[30m]))
```
Note: we actually do a custom aggregation job to compute the "first N requests" window because prom isn't great for request-count windows per-entity.

olivia: That makes sense. Can we annotate the dashboard with the warmup policy (N/time) per row so reviewers understand differences across routes?

mara: Done — added a small metadata column. Also added a heatmap of token-saved per hour.

sre_jen: Any regressed cases from last week's rollout? We saw a drop in hit-rate for rla-*/chat routes.

mara: I instrumented those and found two contributors: 1) A change in key normalization that started trimming trailing whitespace for some legacy routes (good by correctness but changed keys for active customers) and 2) batching heuristic shift that increased sequence-length variance causing fewer identical prefix keys to appear in the same batch so reduced micro-batching cache locality.

dennis: Oof. For (1) can we backfill by mapping old->new keys for a period? For (2) maybe emitting a per-request affinity tag so the runtime keeps similar sequence-length inputs together?

mara: For (1) I added a compatibility layer in the cache lookup: if miss and the route is on the legacy list, we try a secondary lookup using the old-normalization function for 24h. It restored ~85% of the lost hit-rate for impacted customers.

mara: For (2) I'm testing a batching tweak: during the warmup window we bias the sampler to pack short-prefix requests together (increases hit co-location). It's a small change in the batching policy and seems to improve early hit-rate by ~12% in staging.

data_khan: Do you have profiling traces for these staging runs? Would love to see KV lookup latency and kernel selection timelines.

mara: Yes — uploaded traces to the perf-bucket and added thumbnails in the dashboard. The key graph to look at is "kv_lookup_percentile_by_phase" and "kernel_switch_count_per_request".

olivia: Can we add an alert if warmup hit-rate < 30% after N requests for enterprise customers? They care about early latency.

mara: Yup I sketched alert rules:
```
WHEN warmup_hit_rate{customer_tier="enterprise"} < 0.3 FOR 15m
THEN page oncall + create ticket with diagnostic snapshot
```
I left the threshold conservative while we validate.

sre_jen: Also, let's add a per-customer summary export (CSV) so account teams can run quarterly audits.

mara: Export added — includes model, route, warmup_hit_rate, total_tokens_saved, avg_kv_lookup_ms, and variant.

dennis: Great work. One last ask: add a column for "probable key-collision" where we count identical keys across distinct customers to surface multi-tenant collision risks.

mara: Good idea. I'll compute a collision_ratio = collisions / total_unique_keys and show it. I'll run a 7-day backfill and share updated dashboard link.

infra-bot: Deploy report: dashboard changes (dash-182345) applied to grafana:prod at 2026-03-17T10:45:23Z :rocket:

mara: Thanks — leaving this open for 24h to collect feedback before I promote the dashboard to the global "cache-observability" folder. :thumbsup:

olivia: Looks great, will try to poke it with a couple enterprise customers tomorrow.

dennis: LGTM. Thanks for the quick iteration.
